A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same study with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A-G. Content can be matched despite rewriting, table consolidation and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across 32 language models, including probe evaluations, regressions, control validation and critical-edge analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices E-G, including numerical regression results and sentence-level analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same structural, orthogonal structural, head-word and GloVe control probes, with unchanged losses, embedding subtraction and regression procedures. Expanded formulations clarify existing components.

E1.justification: PTB, English BLiMP and the control-validation sample of 500 SimLex-999 words with ten generated contexts each remain unchanged. Newly discussed MultiBLiMP, TurBLiMP and RuBLiMP are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The same three syntax probes and associated control probes participate in the corresponding comparisons. Newly cited work such as CausalGym is discussed without becoming an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Splits, training budgets, layer selection, scoring procedures and Appendix D filtering remain unchanged. GPT-2's label changes from 117M to 124M, but Appendix A identifies the same gpt2 checkpoint; this does not establish a model-configuration change.

E4.justification: Control validation, layerwise and inter-probe comparisons, sentence-level tests and the four critical-edge analyses are retained. The expanded discussion introduces no new ablation, robustness experiment or case-study evidence.

E5.justification: Section 4 explicitly identifies the sentence-level two-sample t-tests as one-sided. v1 already describes the directional hypothesis, so this refines statistical reporting without establishing a changed test. Holm-Bonferroni correction, LRTs and other significance-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All 82 displayed regression rows match after mapping v1 Tables 1-3 and 5-9 to v2 Tables 1 and 3-5. Figure 3 retains its bar values despite rescaling; critical-edge findings and Figure 7 significance counts also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Projection-matrix notation is corrected to agree with the already stated linear maps, and standard UAS/UUAS formulas are made explicit. These are notation and exposition fixes; the losses, regression equations and mathematical reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claim that dependency-probe accuracy fails to reliably predict BLiMP performance across 32 models and three syntax probes. The preference for external targeted evaluations also remains; expanded framing does not redefine the principal contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces multiple testing with accuracy saturation as a possible explanation for the anaphor-agreement correlation. Sections 5 and 7 withdraw v1's extrapolation to other languages and explicitly discuss language-specific effects, alternative probe architectures and the 8B model-size limitation.

D1.justification: The page-2 footnote replaces a promised code release with a concrete repository link. Section 3 explicitly specifies the control probe's 256-dimensional projection and clarifies control-layer associations and regression observations. Appendix B's hardware and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands positioning around causal analysis, probing methodology and multilingual evaluation. It develops comparisons with Belinkov, Ravichander and Elazar, adds CausalGym and multilingual BLiMP references, and replaces the earlier Ruzzetti discussion. These changes extend beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The setup, experimental explanation, results narrative, related work, conclusion and limitations undergo extensive rewriting. v2 separates the critical-edge protocol from regression descriptions, introduces thematic related-work subsections and standardizes BLiMP terminology around paradigms.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 1-3 become v2 Table 1(a-c), and Tables 5-7 become Table 3(a-c). Figure labels, sizing, captions and placement change, and an existing minimal pair gains an annotated display. All 16 numbered figures and their underlying plot designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer procedural explanations, consolidated comparisons and a concrete code link improve usability and reproducibility information. Replacing unsupported cross-language extrapolation with explicit limitations improves calibration. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the new saturation explanation remains conjectural, supporting a limited overall improvement.
